chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Nahiki from Ibn Abi Umayr from a number of our companions from Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Abdullah al-Qasri who said:

I was in Medina, and a boy who had stolen was brought to me. So I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about him. He said: 'Ask him, when he stole, did he know that there was a punishment upon him for the theft? If he says yes, it is said to him: 'What is that punishment?' If he does not know that the punishment for the theft is cutting (of the hand), then free him.'
He said: 'So I took the boy and asked him, and said to him: 'Did you know that there is a punishment for the theft?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'What is it?' He said: 'The whipping.' So I freed him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for imposing the hadd punishment of cutting on a child who steals?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the principle of 'shurut al-hadd' (conditions for the fixed punishment) by linking the severity of the penalty to the child's cognitive awareness of that specific penalty. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights that hadd punishments require not just the act, but the perpetrator's knowledge of the legal consequence, distinguishing between general awareness of wrongdoing and specific knowledge of the corporal penalty. This ruling underscores the mercy and precision in applying hudud to minors who may understand the act but not the full legal weight of it.
